newsitem.title: USA: Falconbridge strike yields no short-term impact.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge strike yields no short-term impact.

text.p: U.S. physical metal traders shrugged off the strike at Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury mine in Ontario, despite a rally in nickel prices on the London Metal Exchange.
Most traders said it was too early to discern any real impact on the physical market, but the potential for harm was greater in the nickel market rather than the copper market.
"We haven't seen any effect yet," said one nickel trader. "It wasn't like the strike was announced and the phone started ringing off the hook. It's going to take some time before we see any impact."
Approximately 1,400 employees represented by the Canadian Auto Workers union walked off the job early Friday after failing to replace a union contract that expired 0800 EDT Friday.
The mine produces 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt.
The copper market responded to the strike with a yawn, in sharp contrast to the Inco Ltd strike two months before which triggered a round of panic buying by U.S. consumers as well as Inco itself.
"The difference is that this time of year there's plenty of copper around," said one physical dealer. "There's no fear of a tightness."
"The strike only affects the smelter," other trader said. "It would take a couple of weeks before we felt the impact on the refined copper end."
The Sudbury complex was on maintanence shutdown at the time the strike was declared, the company said in a statement. It was expected to resume production on Aug. 5.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
